A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphGPT research, with matching authors, method and principal experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v3's added Appendix H.

before.justification: V2 reports original graph-, edge- and node-level benchmark results, component ablations and pre-training loss curves in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds re-indexing ablations, runtime measurements, computational costs and preliminary application results.

M1.justification: The GET backbone, Eulerian serialization, cyclic re-indexing, node identity encoding, NTP/SMTP objectives and downstream task heads are retained. Connecting disconnected components already appears in v2; moving and elaborating that step in v3 clarifies the existing procedure. The additional applications do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: The main benchmarks and pre-training corpora remain unchanged. Appendix H2 additionally reports noisy-graph denoising using the internal corpus already used for pre-training, while H6 reports preliminary molecule generation after PCQM4Mv2 pre-training. Cora and PubMed are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets in Tables 1–5 are retained. V3 adds a runtime comparison against GCN, GIN and their virtual-node variants in Table 17; these methods previously appeared in accuracy comparisons. GraphBERT, GraphMAE and GCC are newly discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported ogbn-arxiv pre-training budget changes from 20 billion tokens with 1 billion warmup tokens in v2 Table 15 to 4 billion and 0.2 billion in v3 Table 16. Table 5 scores remain unchanged, so this does not establish a rerun or same-setting improvement. V3 also adds re-indexing controls at two model sizes and a single-V100 runtime evaluation.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends diagnostic evidence with a controlled node re-indexing ablation (Table 7), runtime comparisons (Table 17), and a noisy-graph case comparing long and short representations (Appendix H2). It replaces PCQM4Mv2 training-loss trajectories in v2 Figure 2 with validation-loss-versus-model-size analyses in v3 Figure 3. Existing pre-training and node identity ablations remain.

E5.justification: V3 newly specifies 10 independent runs for Triangles in Table 3 and Appendix C.3, and reports 3–5 runs for large datasets. V2 already presents uncertainty values but lacks these run counts. This is additional statistical documentation, not evidence that the number of runs increased.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark scores are retained, but reported outcomes expand substantially. V3 adds GraphGPT-M's PCQM4Mv2 validation MAE of 0.0827 and molpcba test AP of 30.13±0.25, re-indexing results, validation-loss scaling plots, and runtime/cost tables. Appendix H additionally reports 10–20% F1 improvement over unnamed denoising baselines and preliminary valid molecule generation, without detailed evaluation settings. The earlier PCQM4Mv2 training trajectories are removed.

T1.justification: V3 adds connectedness to the Eulerian graph definition and introduces a footnote asserting unique NetworkX traversal given a fixed starting node and predetermined indices. These are limited changes to stated mathematical conditions and properties; the reconstruction argument remains and no substantial proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of lossless graph serialization, generative pre-training, unified graph/edge/node prediction, competitive benchmark performance and scaling to two billion parameters. The code-release statement changes access information rather than the central scientific contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations linking stochastic paths and re-indexing to learned invariance and reduced memorization, attributes small-model runtime to CPU preprocessing, and discusses generation dependencies and unresolved adversarial robustness in Appendix H. Section 3.2 narrows its molecular scaling statement from 400M to 200M parameters. The original transferability, dataset-size and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 promises future code and checkpoint release; v3 reports their release and provides access links. V3 also supplies dataset-specific training times and GPU configurations in Table 18, runtime implementation information, additional vocabulary sizes and explicit inference clarification. Together these substantially expand reproducibility and resource information.

R1.justification: Appendix H adds positioning against GraphBERT, GraphMAE and GCC, connects the work to language-model scaling research, and cites adversarial robustness literature. The main related-work narrative remains largely unchanged. Publication updates for existing works, including AGDN and DeeperGCN, do not introduce new comparators.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized rewrites to serialization and implementation explanations, reorganizes connectivity handling, and adds a re-indexing subsection, a twelve-question Appendix H, acknowledgements and an impact statement. The overall introduction-to-conclusion structure and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds a pre-training/fine-tuning diagram, re-indexing and cost tables, and replaces the PCQM4Mv2 trajectory plot with two scaling panels. Table 1 gains explicit method-family labels, captions are expanded, and several displays move. The principal tokenization figure and most existing table and plot designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new re-indexing ablation and runtime/cost tables improve component validation and computational transparency, while run counts and reported code/checkpoint access improve reproducibility documentation. Gains are limited by sparse denoising/generation evidence and an introduced error: Appendix H1 attributes 32.6% accuracy to Triangles pre-training, although Table 3 assigns it to unpretrained GET and reports 92.16% for Triangles-only pre-training. The central benchmark evidence remains stable.
